genZNote: Nicknamed 'Conan the Bacterium' for surviving radiation doses that would shred human DNA thousands of times over — it just repairs the damage and keeps going.

morphology.capsule: Thick cell envelope with multiple layers
morphology.notes: Despite staining Gram-positive, has an unusual multilayered cell envelope with features of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative cells.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, dust, animal feces, and irradiated environments
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Found in dried foods, radioactive waste sites, and other extreme environments where its DNA-repair capability is favored

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive cocci in pairs or tetrads

culture.growthCharacteristics: Aerobic, slow-growing, forms distinctive pink/red colonies
culture.colonyMorphology: Smooth, convex, pink to red-pigmented colonies

identificationClues: Extraordinary resistance to ionizing radiation, desiccation, and UV light due to highly efficient DNA double-strand break repair machinery
Characteristic pink-red carotenoid pigment (deinoxanthin) gives colonies a distinctive color
Forms pairs or tetrads of cocci with an unusual multilayered cell envelope
Not a pathogen — used as a research model for DNA repair and considered for bioremediation of radioactive waste

examFacts.importantTest: Survival/growth after high-dose ionizing radiation exposure
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: One of the most radiation-resistant organisms known, prized as a DNA-repair model and bioremediation candidate

sources.name: NCBI Bookshelf — overview of extremophile bacteria and DNA repair mechanisms
